data.title: Nvidia Faces S&P Downgrade on Governance
data.description:
The Tech Report host Isaac pressed David Gerard on S&P Global Ratings placing Nvidia on watch for a credit downgrade.

Gerard, author and host of Pivot to AI who tracks AI finance, argued Nvidia governance is impaired because Trump forced Jensen Huang back.

Gerard said Trump called into the Nvidia board meeting on Sunday to guarantee no security problem and even discussed pardoning Huang.

Credit judges whether Nvidia can repay debt while stock only bets price will rise, Gerard said.

Bloomberg reported S&P is weighing a one notch cut after Huang left and returned, a detail Gerard tied to key man risk.

Gerard said Nvidia shares rose for one day after Huang returned then fell again as Oracle slipped toward junk.

Lenders still ask if Nvidia can service debt even when traders bid shares higher, Gerard warned.

data.title: iFood turned 15,000 repos into API calls
data.description:
OpenAI says iFood now fixes code by API call and gets back a merge request. The Remote Agents Platform covers more than 15,000 repositories, according to the company.

Stop watching the bot work.

Each run clones the repo, loads skills, cuts a branch, runs GPT-5.6 Luna in an isolated Ubuntu sandbox, then ships artifacts and a merge request, with more than 25,000 runs completed at US$0.04 per run according to iFood. "Solving this for one repository is easy. The challenge is solving it at scale," says Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer at iFood, who says teams keep business logic and hand off execution.

Security took it first. Its scanner hunts vulnerable dependencies across those repos, and iFood says fixes more than doubled after the move, with Structured Outputs forcing each session into a pass or fail contract.

iFood says it copied the OpenAI Agents API and Batch API for async design. That lineage tracks, since OpenAI launched the Responses API and open-source Agents SDK together in March 2025, with Responses as a superset of Chat Completions, per eesel AI.

You still do not watch dependency bumps in a meeting. You still own the judgment calls the contract cannot grade, and at four cents a run the constraint shifts from headcount to which chores you trust.

data.title: Google AI Answers Cost French Sites 24% of Clicks
data.description:
Did Google's AI answers really erase a quarter of search clicks in France? Ahrefs says yes, with a net 24.4% click-through rate loss three months after launch.

The control group proves it is not seasonal.

An AI Overview is the AI-written answer Google places above classic results to answer the query directly. Google rolled it out in France, according to Ahrefs. Coverage jumped from 0% of tracked keywords in June to 88.5% by November 25, with a 35.4 point jump in August alone, according to Ahrefs.

Ahrefs compared 31,612 French keywords between June and October 2026, per its methodology. Ahrefs found keywords that gained an AI Overview fell from 2.53% CTR to 1.964%, a 22.4% drop, while keywords without one rose 2.6%. Had affected keywords followed that trend they would have hit 2.596%, so observed versus expected is a 24.4% net loss, according to Ahrefs.

No rank is safe. Ahrefs says every position lost more than 20% CTR from June to September 2026, with position one falling from 11.06% to 8.69%. Against a control that rose to 11.78%, the net loss at position one is 26.2%, not 21.4%, according to Ahrefs.

So does intent save commercial pages? Not really. Ahrefs reports informational and navigational queries lost about 25% net CTR and commercial and transactional queries lost about 20%. That early August signal still holds, when 963 domains lost 3.4% CTR in nine days overall and 82.2% of highly exposed domains lost clicks, per Keywords Everywhere citing Ahrefs data scientist Xibeijia Guan.

Intent softens the hit by four to five points.

France gives planners a 25% rule

That leaves the SEO lead with new math. Find AI Overview queries in Ahrefs Site Explorer with the SERP features filter, then apply a 25% CTR cut to their traffic share, as Ahrefs advises. If 40% of traffic comes from those queries, expect about a 10% sitewide loss at constant impressions, so watch that share weekly as coverage spreads.

data.title: Sakana Marlin adds Twilight and Midnight modes
data.description:
Sakana AI added Twilight 2.0 and Midnight 2.0 to Sakana Marlin. The company says Twilight grabs structure fast and Midnight chases depth and verification in its Marlin update.

Sunlight stays as the cheap, light option.

Sakana AI charges 100 credits for Sunlight and 300 for Twilight 2.0 or Midnight 2.0, the company said. Twilight finishes more than an hour sooner than Sunlight while pulling about 3 times as many sources, the company said. Midnight pulls about 7 times as many sources and produces about 5 times the report volume, the company said. It's inference-time scaling tied to process, not just longer output.

Sakana AI argues thinking longer is not thinking better without a way to judge good research. The new modes reframe questions and retest hypotheses as they dig, the company said.

That is a different bet from its Namazu Small push.

The Tokyo lab builds around nature-inspired intelligence and pitched Namazu Small, a 30B model, against Nvidia Nemotron 3 Super and Nano on long-document grounding, per AI Chat Daily. Slides got a rebuild too, with an agent harness that reads the full report, picks a story, builds charts and checks its own output, the company said. Decks now open with cover, contents and executive summary and carry source URLs, but you won't know how clean those auto-built charts look until you try your own template.

Sakana AI did not say how it scores good research when no single answer exists. What counts as verified when the agent grades its own homework?

data.title: Crusoe caps per-VM RDMA memory after hidden use hit 6 GiB
data.description:
Crusoe said it set a per-VF firmware budget for RDMA context after heavy GPU VMs pushed one NIC to 6 GiB of hidden host RAM. Typical VMs stay under 1 GiB per NIC, Crusoe said.

Disaggregated inference and expert-parallel MoE training drive the spikes, Crusoe said. A single TCP worker peaks at 8 to 10 Gbit/s regardless of chunk size, per LMCache measurements, so teams move payloads to RDMA.

Each registration looks free inside the guest.

The affected systems are Crusoe GPU VMs with NVIDIA ConnectX-7 InfiniBand adapters passed as SR-IOV VFs, eight VFs per host, Crusoe said. No remote exploit is needed, since a local guest can exhaust host memory with normal verbs, Crusoe said. Each translation entry costs 8 bytes per mapped page, Crusoe said, so one 265 GiB registration costs about 530 MiB at 4 KiB pages, about 33 MiB at 64 KiB pages and about 1 MiB at 2 MiB pages, Crusoe said.

Crusoe said it tracks hidden pages with a per-NIC fw_pages_total counter read once a minute into Prometheus. The host applies the VF budget on every boot and guests cannot change it, with direct support on DOCA 3.2.x and a validated workaround on DOCA 2.9.x, Crusoe said. Over budget, a 40 GiB ibv_reg_dmabuf_mr failed with Resource temporarily unavailable, or EAGAIN, while existing queues kept passing traffic, Crusoe said.

Teams running disaggregated inference, MoE all-to-all or large collectives must register only buffers moved over RDMA and check mkey page size with rdma resource show, Crusoe said. Fragmented buffers force 4 KiB pages and need 512 times more entries than 2 MiB pages for the same bytes, Crusoe said. A running VM keeps its budget until workload restart, and the host reapplies it on every boot, Crusoe said.

data.title: Lean checked a GRH proof, no human has read it
data.description:
lsernau published a shortened Lean 4 formalization, which is machine-checked mathematics that the Lean proof assistant verifies step by step, that claims to prove the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.

The Riemann Hypothesis is the claim that the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function all lie on one line. The generalized version extends that claim to Dirichlet L-functions, which are twisted analogues of the zeta function tied to arithmetic characters. Scientific American reported that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he proved it with a large language model, which is an AI system trained to predict text. The problem is 167 years old, per Clarin, which explains why a machine check draws attention.

lsernau offers two editions with the same five theorems. The readable edition in grh/ runs about 300,000 lines and starts at grh/GUIDE.md, lsernau says. The compact edition in grh-compact/ runs about 76,000 lines for the same five theorems, lsernau says. Each folder is its own Lake project, which is Lean’s build and package system, and each pins Lean v4.35.0 and Mathlib at commit 56a00585, lsernau says, where Mathlib is Lean’s shared library of formalized mathematics.

A rebuild follows the order a Lean user expects. You fetch the cache with lake exe cache get, then run lake build, then check dependencies with lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean. lsernau says a build takes one to two hours on 12 cores with 24 GB of memory, plus about 85 minutes if the Mathlib cache is missing. The expected axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, lsernau says.

Machine checking is not peer review. lsernau says the proof has passed machine checks only, no mathematician has read it through, and no paper comes with it. The repository is marked as a research artifact, not maintained and not accepting contributions. If you have the hardware, you can rebuild it now and watch for an independent reading or a paper that explains the mathematical move.

data.title: 1Password Breach Takes Names, Not Vaults
data.description:
1Password says a remote attacker used an employee corporate GitHub account to reach backend systems and copy account records for a subset of customers.

The company said it began investigating after finding the GitHub access, source code theft and malicious code pushed to backend services that pulled administrative data. That pull took names and sign-in emails, account and user identifiers, creation and last sign-in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password parameters and tokens from certain emailed invite and recovery links, plus internal numeric metadata.

The vaults held.

1Password said vault contents, vault keys, account passwords, Secret Keys, recovery keys and apps were not affected, a zero-knowledge design it has documented since 2015. That separation is the pitch against Apple Passwords and Bitwarden on buyer shortlists, where the test is not if servers are touched but if touched servers yield secrets. Macworld, the consumer tech outlet, reported the access itself happened November 19, while 1Password says November 19 is when investigation began, and called the loss admin data, a term the company did not use.

1Password said it disabled the GitHub account, revoked the token, rotated internal credentials, expanded invite codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits and brought in outside experts, with no evidence of takeovers using exposed provisioning tokens. It did not say how the GitHub token was stolen, how many customers sit in the subset, or how long the malicious code ran before containment?

data.title: Databricks says hijacked npm packages drove 99% of downloads
data.description:
Databricks says it tracked 5,400 confirmed malicious npm packages published between December 2025 and October 2026, the first year after npm revoked long-lived tokens. Compromised legitimate packages were 7% of the set but drove over 99% of downloads, per Databricks. Attacker-created packages were 89% of the set and 0.2% of downloads, per Databricks. The set includes only packages with an advisory, takedown or analyst review, per Databricks. Not financial advice. Markets move fast.

The exposure is not where the volume is.

Authors Alessandra Rizzo, Panos Sakkos and Ariel Ropek, writing for Databricks Threat Research, said the shift ran through build pipelines after token revocation. Of packages in the set published via trusted publishing, 85% are compromised legitimate packages, per Databricks. Attacker-created packages used trusted publishing in 0.1% of cases, the team said. The August 2026 worm republished high-exposure victims through OIDC from compromised CI, per the report.

Databricks said a distinct set now targets AI developer tooling, including MCP servers that harvest host credentials and packages that rewrite assistant config files. That matches warnings outside the dataset. CybersecurityNews reported that attackers can scan exposed MCP tools and use compromised credentials to reach connected resources. Centeye Security reported that a malicious copy of a real email MCP server was found in 2025 and a flaw in a popular MCP tool let a server run code on the connecting laptop. One frames it as endpoint exposure, the other as registry distribution.

Databricks said 38% of malicious packages called a legitimate shared service, from serverless hosting to chat webhooks and paste sites, so domain reputation did not separate bad traffic. Public advisories covered 87% of confirmed packages at a median 1.7 days after publication, the company said. Registry takedown followed at a median 7 days, with 10% over 59 days, per the same analysis. Attackers unpublished 37% of attacker-created packages themselves in a median seven hours, Databricks said. About 16% remained installable as of the registry check, per the report.

Rizzo, Sakkos and Ropek declined to assign responsibility for blocking installs during that gap. They also did not say how registries should handle npm as free hosting for payloads that never need an install. Who pays for faster takedowns when hijacked builds carry 99% of the risk and vanish in hours?

data.title: OpenAI wants your dot to cover on-call
data.description:
OpenAI wants your dot to cover on-call while you take the holiday weekend off.

Dot understands what matters because it connects to where you work, OpenAI said. You can tell it to follow key threads, keep a log of what comes in and ping you only if something is critical. It can also act alone, turning customer channel feedback into a Linear ticket without a prompt.

The demo goes further for engineering. You ask the dot to watch on-call notifications, investigate each issue and report back. It spots the alert, opens a Codex thread to run code and tests, then sends an update you can steer from your phone. When a fix is ready, you ask the dot to check the original report against the staging build and show what passed or failed before you ship.

That background role is the shift. OpenAI describes dot as an always-on agent in ChatGPT with its own cloud computer that keeps making progress between conversations. Engadget reported OpenAI is testing Dots on its $20 per month Plus tier, which puts supervised autonomy in a consumer plan rather than a separate enterprise tool.

The demo does not show accuracy, false alert rate or permission limits. Independent data on how many incidents it resolves without human edits would change the read. Will teams let a phone-steered fix ship while the owner stays away?
